The greatest common factor (GCF) of 6432 and 132 is found using the Euclidean algorithm:

- \(6432 \div 132 = 48\) remainder \(96\), so \(6432 = 132 \times 48 + 96\).
- \(132 \div 96 = 1\) remainder \(36\), so \(132 = 96 \times 1 + 36\).
- \(96 \div 36 = 2\) remainder \(24\), so \(96 = 36 \times 2 + 24\).
- \(36 \div 24 = 1\) remainder \(12\), so \(36 = 24 \times 1 + 12\).
- \(24 \div 12 = 2\) remainder \(0\), so the GCF is \(12\).

Alternatively, prime factorization confirms: \(6432 = 2^5 \times 3 \times 67\), \(132 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 11\); common factors are \(2^2 \times 3 = 12\).

Increasing the GCF by 11 gives \(12 + 11 = 23\).

Answer: 23
